edges.description: Autism in the index proband is curated as one presentation of the behavioral arm of the neurodevelopmental phenotype.
Convergent strabismus is grouped with the brain-development arm as a neuro-ophthalmologic finding accompanying optic atrophy. Reported in one individual; the causal route is not established.

The optic nerve is a central nervous system tract, so optic atrophy is grouped with the brain-development arm on anatomical grounds. Reported in one affected individual; the causal route is not established, hence UNKNOWN rather than an asserted indirect causal link.

Feeding difficulty and dysphagia in this disorder are attributed to the central hypotonia and bulbar dysfunction of the neurodevelopmental arm; no intrinsic gastrointestinal pathology has been established as their cause.
Swallowing difficulty is attributed to the same central hypotonia and bulbar dysfunction as the feeding difficulty, rather than to a structural gastrointestinal lesion.

Postnatal growth failure is placed on this arm rather than the multisystem arm because its documented proximate cause in this disorder is the feeding difficulty and dysphagia arising from central hypotonia and bulbar dysfunction.

The musculoskeletal arm is the one with independent molecular corroboration: the shared aberrantly spliced gene set is enriched for musculoskeletal as well as nervous-system phenotype terms, and WBP4 is expressed most highly in skeletal and cardiac muscle.

Grouped with the craniofacial/multisystem arm because the inner ear is a craniofacial developmental derivative. Reported in one individual; the causal route is not established, hence UNKNOWN rather than an asserted indirect causal link.

Prenatal growth restriction is grouped here as the earliest multisystem growth manifestation, preceding the postnatal failure to thrive. This is a temporal and organizational grouping, not a demonstrated causal step, hence UNKNOWN.

Grouped with the multisystem arm only because recurrent infection was reported in the same individual who had the multisystem malformation burden. No immune evaluation was reported, no mechanism has been proposed, and no causal claim is made here - the link type is UNKNOWN.

edges.limitations: Fibroblasts are a mesenchymal skin-derived cell type, not a neural one. Splice-site usage is cell-type dependent, so a nervous-system phenotype enrichment computed on the fibroblast transcriptome is an indirect proxy for what happens in developing brain. The probands' fibroblasts were also compared against adult parental fibroblasts, and the authors themselves attribute an unexplained skin-phenotype enrichment in the differential-expression analysis to that age mismatch rather than to disease biology.

nodes.description: WBP4 (FBP21) is a 376-amino-acid protein with a zinc finger motif and two tandem WW domains that is present exclusively in the spliceosomal B complex, acting immediately before catalytic activation. Biochemical and biophysical work on the protein shows that an intrinsically disordered region binds the C-terminal Sec63 unit of the RNA helicase Brr2 (SNRNP200) and allosterically inhibits its helicase activity, and that direct binding of the protein to the U4/U6 di-snRNA reduces the pool of unwound U4/U6. Because SNRNP200-driven U4/U6 unwinding is the irreversible commitment step of the B-to-Bact transition, losing this brake is expected to alter the kinetics of catalytic activation and hence splice-site selection. The node is marked PROVISIONAL because the biochemical inhibition was characterized in reconstituted systems, and de-repression of SNRNP200 has not been measured directly in WBP4-null patient cells. The biochemical evidence is therefore curated as PARTIAL for this disease-state node rather than as direct support.

nodes.description: Human-phenotype enrichment analysis of the 619 genes aberrantly spliced in both probands returned abnormalities of the nervous system and of the musculoskeletal system, matching the probands' shared clinical features. Aberrantly spliced genes with the strongest phenotype match include NFIX, TRIO, ANKRD11, SZT2, HUWE1, PIGT, SMARCC2, PEX1, QRICH1 and HRAS, together with SMARCA2, HNRNPH1 and TCF4 - all established neurodevelopmental-disease genes. Seven of the top ten are autosomal dominant genes, which the authors interpret as consistent with partial (dosage-like) mis-splicing mimicking a dominant effect. The node is PROVISIONAL because the enrichment is a statistical association computed in fibroblasts, not a demonstration that any individual transcript is functionally deficient in a patient's brain.

nodes.description: RNA sequencing of primary fibroblasts from two unrelated WBP4-null probands versus their heterozygous parents identified 5,675 differential splicing events in 2,859 genes in the first proband and 2,868 events in 1,555 genes in the second. meta.association: Homozygous loss-of-function variants in WBP4 cause this disorder. Five distinct alleles were identified across eight unrelated families ascertained through GeneMatcher, with segregation consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance in the families tested, and all alleles absent or present at extremely low frequency in population databases. Functional support is direct: complete absence of WBP4 protein in patient fibroblasts and a shared aberrant splicing signature in two unrelated probands carrying different alleles. WBP4 had not previously been associated with any human phenotype in OMIM.

evidence.snippet: WW domain-binding protein 4 (WBP4) is part of the early spliceosomal complex and has not been previously associated with human pathologies in the Online Mendelian Inheritance in Man (OMIM) database.

nodes.description: Homozygous frameshift variant identified in two affected siblings from a consanguineous family (chr13:g.41072793 GA>G, hg38), predicted to result in a premature stop codon. Absent from gnomAD. WBP4 mRNA was reduced in this proband, consistent with nonsense-mediated decay, and WBP4 protein was undetectable on immunoblot of his fibroblasts.

evidence.reference_title: Biallelic loss of function variants in WBP4, encoding a spliceosome protein, result in a variable neurodevelopmental delay syndrome.
evidence.snippet: This variant is absent from the Genome Aggregation Database (gnomAD), and no other homozygous LOF variant in this gene was described before.

nodes.description: Homozygous deletion removing the three terminal exons of WBP4 (chr13:41,074,140-41,090,168, hg38), located within a ~6.2 Mb region of loss of heterozygosity. Initially missed by trio exome analysis and detected only after RNA sequencing showed very low WBP4 expression, prompting reanalysis of genome data; confirmed by Sanger sequencing. The residual transcript terminates at exon 7 of 10 and no protein is detectable. Carried by the most severely affected individual, who had VACTERL association and died prematurely.

evidence.snippet: Homozygous deletion of the three last exons of the WBP4 gene was validated by Sanger sequencing.

evidence.reference_title: Biallelic loss of function variants in WBP4, encoding a spliceosome protein, result in a variable neurodevelopmental delay syndrome.
evidence.snippet: RNA sequencing revealed a very low expression of the WBP4 gene (Figure S3), and reanalysis of genome data indicated a homozygous deletion in this region (Figure S4).

nodes.description: Primary dermal fibroblasts obtained by skin biopsy from two unrelated affected individuals (one homozygous frameshift, one homozygous multi-exon deletion) and from their heterozygous parents, with an independent wild-type fibroblast line as control. Used for immunoblotting of WBP4 and for RNA sequencing with differential-expression (DESeq2) and differential-splicing (rMATS) analysis. This is the only experimental system in which the disease mechanism has been studied; no animal or stem-cell-derived model of WBP4 loss exists.
